notesStmt.note: The additions and corrections on this proof were made sometime between June 20, 1883, when Whitman received the invitation to write a poem, and August 5, 1883, when the letter was published. The date, significance, and intended recipient of the notes at the bottom of the scrap are unknown.

A partial proof of a letter, with handwritten additions and corrections. Sevreal other copies of the full proof are extant (see, for example, duk.00727 and hun.00067). The letter was published in its entirety in the Philadelphia Press on August 5, 1883, with the following headnote: "Our friends at Santa Fé, New Mexico, have just finish'd​ their long drawn out anniversary of the 333d year of the settlement of their city by the Spanish. The good, gray Walt Whitman was asked to write them a poem in commemoration. Instead he wrote them a letter as follows." On June 20, 1883, Whitman had received an invitation from Arthur Boyle, requesting a poem for the "Santa Fé Tertio Millennial Celebration." Whitman reprinted the letter and the headnote in November Boughs (1888) under the title "The Spanish Element in Our Nationality."

body.p: If I might assume to do so, I would like to send you the most cordial, hertfelt, respectful congratulations of your American fellow-countrymen here. You have more friends in the Northern and Atlantic regions than you suppose, and they are deeply interested in the development of the great Southwestern interior, and in what your festival would arouse to public attention.
